correctness.rationale: The identity T=2R−I and the positive semigroup integral for R leave only diagonal entries to check. Walsh eigenvalues are 2w(S), so the common diagonal is the stated F_w. Its limit 2^(−r) and strict decrease give the cutoff, including +infinity at r=1. For h>0 the strict convexity of (1+hz)^−1 on z≥0 gives strict increase of the pair terms with spread, including boundary weights; a finite chain of majorization transfers proves the strict order up to permutations. Deleting a uniformly selected Bernoulli trial produces the smaller sample-mean law with the larger mean as its conditional mean, with strict inequality by Jensen on nonconstant samples. The centered second, fourth and sixth moments give a uniform expansion with remainder O(d^−3); the reciprocal terms through degree four give the coefficients 1 and 5/4 after root inversion, because the slope stays bounded away from zero near 2. Independent binomial bisection gave t_2≈3.2360679775 and t_1024≈2.000977756225; these are finite corroboration, not the proof. Clearing the positive denominators gives the stated cubic. With p=ab and h_0=sqrt(2/p), the positive root is h_0+u with 4u+3p h_0 u²+p u³=2/W, hence 0<u≤1/(2W) and u=1/(2W)+O_W(sqrt(a)). The frozen script was inspected, not run.
